business_problem: de la Fuente Lab needed a faster, less trial-and-error way to discover antibiotic candidates against antimicrobial resistance because traditional molecule hunting can take years and requires difficult computational work across multiple scientific disciplines.
solution_summary: de la Fuente Lab uses ChatGPT and Codex as an AI-assisted discovery environment for antimicrobial research. The team treats DNA and molecular biology as code, feeds discovery questions and experimental ideas into ChatGPT, and uses the model to help formulate algorithms that can search complex biological systems for promising antibiotic candidates. Codex then turns those ideas into scripts, plotting routines, and computational biology workflows that chemists, biologists, and engineers across the lab can actually run. Candidate molecules move from AI-assisted analysis into wet-lab synthesis and testing, creating a loop where computational suggestions inform experiments and lab results shape the next search. This setup lets the lab work at digital speed, shortens the path from hypothesis to candidate discovery, and broadens who can contribute to computational biology inside the team.

solution_components.name: ChatGPT
solution_components.role: Helps researchers generate ideas and devise algorithms for identifying antibiotic candidates from biological data.

solution_components.name: Codex
solution_components.role: Turns research ideas into scripts and analysis workflows the lab can use for computational biology work.

data_flow: Researchers frame molecular discovery problems in ChatGPT, turn promising approaches into code with Codex, run those workflows across biological data and molecular structures, and then pass the resulting candidates into wet-lab testing to validate which molecules can kill pathogens.
business_outcome: The lab dramatically accelerated candidate discovery, enabled more non-programmers to participate in computational biology, and increased confidence that AI-assisted research can uncover life-saving antibiotic molecules.
